findings.message: Invalid `-n` values exit with status 1 and omit the command usage line. The README conventions require invalid option arguments to use the usage-error format and exit 2; route this through `lk_usage_error number "invalid start: $OPTARG"`.

`$@` is unquoted here, so filenames containing spaces are split and wildcard characters may expand before `lk_check_files` validates them. This can reject valid input files or validate different paths from those passed to awk. Use `"$@"`.

parsed.summary: The new option has an inconsistent usage-error path, and the file validation call breaks handling of filenames with spaces or wildcard characters.

pull_request.title: number: add -n START to begin numbering at START
pull_request.body:
Adds `-n START` to `linekit number`, so a numbered excerpt can keep the line numbers of the file it was cut from:

    sed -n 120,140p f | linekit number -n 120

The command table in README.md is updated.
